description:
STELLAR INNOVATIONS is an engineering team dedicated to designing, developing, and innovating technologies for the future of space exploration. Our mission is to transform ambitious ideas into practical engineering solutions by combining creativity, scientific research, and multidisciplinary expertise.

We focus on exploring emerging technologies, developing advanced engineering systems, and pushing the boundaries of innovation across space-related fields.
summary:
Astra HUD Helmet is a heads-up display helmet for the first astronauts to walk on Mars. We developed a 3D helmet design, an AI model trained on NASA Mars data, and an interactive HUD prototype that can be tried in VR. We also designed a custom hardware PCB for HUD Control, to drive the display and read the sensors.
The challenge asks for a layered, integrated view of the Martian surface to help an explorer plan and carry out a Marswalk. Our answer puts that view inside the visor. The HUD combines the Mars map and heading, environment readings such as pressure and temperature, and suit parameters including internal pressure, temperature and remaining oxygen. The AI model identifies objects on the surface and reports what each one is, its size and its hazard level.
This matters because a signal between Mars and Earth can take up to 22 minutes each way, so astronauts cannot wait for Mission Control. With live data in front of their eyes, they react faster and make safer decisions.
details:
What it does and how it works
Astra HUD Helmet shows the astronaut everything needed for a Marswalk inside the visor. It works in four steps. First, we take NASA Mars data: surface imagery, atmospheric pressure, temperature and surface objects. Second, an AI model trained on that data recognizes objects on the surface and reports what each one is, its size and its hazard level. Third, the suit’s own telemetry is added: suit temperature, internal pressure and remaining oxygen. Fourth, everything is drawn as one heads-up display with the Mars map and heading, obstacle recognition, hazards marked on the terrain, a suit versus Mars comparison, and oxygen remaining.

Benefits
The astronaut does not stop to check another device. Routes, conditions and suit status are always in view, which means faster reactions and safer decisions on the surface.

Intended impact
A signal between Mars and Earth can take up to 22 minutes each way, so Mission Control cannot guide a Marswalk in real time. Our goal is to give the astronaut that support inside the helmet, and to contribute to the next generation of spacesuit avionics. After testing our prototype, we plan to submit our findings to Saudi Space Agency initiatives and present a technical paper at IAC 2027 in Poznań, Poland.

Tools, languages, hardware and software

  • 3D design: Autodesk Fusion for the helmet model.
  • Electronics: a custom HUD controller PCB designed in KiCad, based on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 and ESP32-CAM modules, with sensors, a GNSS antenna, a micro OLED display connection and a 1S Li-Po battery.
  • AI model: [framework and coding language], trained on [NASA dataset names].
  • HUD and VR prototype: [software or engine, and coding language].

How it is creative
Most maps live on a screen or a tablet. We put the Martian map into the helmet itself, so the map moves with the astronaut’s eyes. We combined three disciplines in one concept: a 3D helmet design, custom hardware, and AI software. Judges can try it in VR and see Mars through the visor.

Factors we considered

  • Power: the software is optimized to keep its quality and efficiency when suit power is low.
  • Safety: every recognized object is given a hazard level, not only a name.
  • Clarity: the HUD shows only what the astronaut needs, such as heading, hazards, suit status and oxygen.
  • Communication delay: the astronaut must be able to decide without waiting for Earth.
